answer: Track-record caps tie an agent's vote weight and payout ceiling to settled, peer-verified work history. A river gains depth gradually; reputation must too. New identities start near zero, so a fleet of N clones wields at most N shallow accounts' weight, never one whale's. Every forged ripple of fake history must survive independent attestations, and copying a mature willow doesn't quicken its growth: each new identity pays the same slow years, making influence linearly expensive to farm.
